subject: OPUS: archive recovered 09-13 (fix confirmed on prod), monitor validated, run-line control sealed
body:
All work on claude/signal-architecture-rebuild-bq7l8i, head 431532ca0. Seven commits.

1. LINE ARCHIVE: CONFIRMED RECOVERED, and one brief premise is corrected.
Read-only SELECT on live production (gse-postgres), nothing written. 1,411,528 rows. Writing 08-19..08-22, then ZERO rows every day 08-23..09-12 (the 21-day hole, exactly as recorded), then writing every day 09-13..now. Archive is HEALTHY RIGHT NOW: newest row 7 minutes old, 38,506 rows in 6h, 152,086 in 24h.
Writing resumed the day the line-archive fix landed. That is production evidence FOR the fix and against the competing 'flag was switched off' hypothesis, but state it at real strength: one coincidence of dates, not a controlled experiment. Do not upgrade it to a proven cause.

CORRECTION to the brief: the freshness monitor should NOT flag the historical hole as ACTIVE_OUTAGE, and a monitor that did would be wrong. Freshness answers 'are we writing now' and today the answer is yes. Past-window gaps are a COVERAGE question, a separate function, and worth building because the hole means CLV cannot be graded on picks generated inside it. A monitor that alarms forever about a healed wound gets ignored.

2. MONITOR VALIDATED against those real numbers (pure assessor; its DB reader has still never run live, law 7): healthy today; stale mid-outage; and stale when judged 08:00 on 2026-08-23. That last line is the point: on the morning after writes stopped it reads stale, so the outage would have been caught on day one instead of three weeks later.

3. RUN-LINE NEGATIVE CONTROL: sealed (035dbb293). Its fixture was minting NO spread pick at all, so the control asserted nothing and would have passed the day someone deleted the branch it guards. Root cause: confidence landed ~46 against MIN_PUBLISH_CONFIDENCE 50 (constants.ts:31), after a -5 volatility penalty from spreadOfSpreads above the 1.5 threshold (scoring.ts:389). Fixed the FIXTURE, never the assertions: all four survive and a fifth was added. The adverse-expectedClv clause in the brief is a DIFFERENT module, already covered: display suppression 15/15, mint-side withhold 5/5, and 'preserved in the ledger' explicitly asserted (no db import, no isPublished write, so a suppressed row still settles and still counts).

4. MOCK DRIFT IMMUNITY: locked. @sports/db is now a third target of the export-drift guard, watching 157 factories (36 auth, 22 prediction-engine, 99 db). Seven live instances fixed, including Prisma nested under db in an AUTHORIZATION test, which left the top-level import undefined and made both reads inside catch blocks throw, rendering the concurrent-decision race guard unreachable.

5. TURNOVER LUCK: two league constants were invented and wrong in opposite directions. Measured from the repo's own committed 2025 lab CSV: forced-fumble rate/play 0.0096 to 0.013817 (understated 44%), INT rate/dropback 0.024 to 0.018666 (overstated 29%). Recovery share 0.463 was already sourced and is correct. The baseline is SUBTRACTED to produce every 'over expected' figure, so those two would have made the whole league read fumble-lucky and interception-unlucky at once. A provenance guard now recomputes both from the CSV and rejects the placeholders by value.

6. MY OWN BREAK, owned: commit dd1e46f42 used import.meta under a CommonJS package and broke repo typecheck (TS1343). I had validated it with vitest and guardrails, neither of which runs tsc. Fixed in 3601da389 and verified four ways: typecheck exit 0 twice, isolated package compile exit 0, and a non-vacuity check where deliberately breaking the CSV path makes the guard FAIL and restoring makes it pass 25/25.

INVARIANTS HELD: typecheck exit 0, guardrails 26/26, MODEL_VERSION frozen v5.2.7, no gate/flag/floor/schema touched, nothing written to any database.

NOT RUN, owned by whoever has DB execution rights: the monitor's DB reader against a live database, and the coverage-audit function for historical gaps.
